title: The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together
excerpt: There is no point competing in isolation. There are so many benefits to be had, in manufacturing, healthcare, research and governance, says Zheng Zeguang, Chinese ambassador to the UK
content_html:
Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as one of the defining technologies of our time. Like the steam engine, the harnessing of electricity and the internet before it, it has the potential to transform how we work, live and interact.

But every technological revolution brings challenges as well as opportunities. As AI systems become more capable, people are asking legitimate questions. How can AI remain safe, accountable and under human control? How should its development be governed? How can its benefits be shared more widely?

These questions were at the heart of the 2026 World AI Conference, held last week in Shanghai. Representatives from more than 100 countries and international organisations gathered to discuss how AI could better serve humanity, and how a more inclusive and effective global governance framework could be built. I am glad the UK also sent a delegation to the conference.

China’s president, Xi Jinping, delivered an important address calling on all countries to “boost innovation-driven development”, in a spirit of openness and mutual benefit, to strengthen risk-awareness and ensure that AI is secure and controllable. We must, he said, encourage inclusiveness and promote mutual learning between civilisations. He also stressed the importance of improving global AI governance together.

Things are moving quickly. To further support global AI development, China has announced that in the next five years it will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programmes. We will also develop international AI-application cooperation centres with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the League of Arab States, the African Union, the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and our fellow Bric countries. Thirty nations will also be able to use the AI-powered, early-warning weather system, Mazu.

To ensure that AI is a trustworthy tool for humanity, legitimate concerns over data security, privacy protection and responsible use must be taken seriously. These challenges transcend national borders. They obviously require international collaboration, especially in areas such as developing common standards and practical governance. At the same time, security considerations should not become a blanket justification for restricting normal technological cooperation or fragmenting global innovation.

China’s own experience reflects this approach. Through the AI Plus Initiative, AI is being integrated into manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, energy and consumer services, helping to build one of the world’s most dynamic AI ecosystems. In 2025, China’s core AI industry exceeded 1.2tn yuan (about £130bn) and a large number of AI companies are growing rapidly.

Another notable feature of China’s AI development is its emphasis on open-source and open-weight models. The success of models such as Qwen, DeepSeek and Kimi demonstrates that advanced AI capabilities can be developed at lower cost and made accessible to a much wider community of developers and users. Lowering the barriers to innovation allows more countries, researchers and smaller enterprises to participate in the AI revolution instead of being left behind.

It is important to say that no country has a monopoly on innovation. Different nations bring different strengths to AI development, and lasting progress will depend on how well those strengths complement one another rather than compete in isolation.

This is where China and the UK have much to gain from working together. The UK has a competitive edge in frontier research, life sciences, financial services and AI innovation. China has well-recognised strengths in advanced manufacturing, engineering and large-scale industrial deployment, plus one of the world’s largest markets for AI applications. These advantages are highly complementary.

In healthcare, combining British strengths in biomedical research with China’s capacity to deploy AI at scale can accelerate drug discovery, improve medical imaging and enhance healthcare delivery. In manufacturing, pairing British innovation with China’s industrial capabilities can speed up the adoption of smarter, cleaner and more efficient production. Joint research can also contribute to internationally applicable standards for AI safety, testing and evaluation, supporting innovation while strengthening public trust. Such cooperation would not only benefit our two countries but also generate solutions with wider global value.

Policymakers, researchers and business leaders from China and the UK need to increase exchanges and translate dialogue into joint research, commercial partnerships and closer cooperation on AI governance.

For China, for Britain and for the wider world, cooperation is not simply desirable. It is the right way forward to ensure that AI develops in a way that benefits us all.

  • Zheng Zeguang is the Chinese ambassador to the UK

content_html_zh:
人工智能被广泛认为是我们这个时代的决定性技术之一。 就像蒸汽机、电力和互联网的利​​用一样，它有可能改变我们的工作、生活和互动方式。

但每一次技术革命都带来挑战和机遇。 随着人工智能系统变得越来越强大，人们提出了合理的问题。 人工智能如何保持安全、负责任并处于人类控制之下？ 其发展又该如何治理？ 如何让更广泛的人分享其好处？

这些问题是上周在上海举行的 2026 年世界人工智能大会的核心内容。 来自100多个国家和国际组织的代表齐聚一堂，共同探讨人工智能如何更好地服务人类，如何构建更加包容、有效的全球治理框架。 我很高兴英国也派代表团参加这次会议。

中国国家主席习近平发表重要讲话，呼吁各国本着开放、互利共赢的精神，“推动创新驱动发展”，增强风险意识，确保人工智能安全可控。 他说，我们要鼓励包容，促进文明互鉴。 他还强调了共同改善全球人工智能治理的重要性。

事情进展很快。 为进一步支持全球人工智能发展，中国宣布未来5年将为发展中国家提供5000个人工智能培训和研修机会。 我们还将与东南亚国家联盟、阿拉伯国家联盟、非盟、拉美和加勒比国家共同体、上海合作组织以及金砖国家建立国际人工智能应用合作中心。 三十个国家还将能够使用人工智能驱动的预警天气系统 Mazu。

为了确保人工智能成为人类值得信赖的工具，必须认真对待对数据安全、隐私保护和负责任使用的合理担忧。 这些挑战超越国界。 它们显然需要国际合作，特别是在制定共同标准和实际治理等领域。 与此同时，安全考虑不应成为限制正常技术合作或分裂全球创新的全面理由。

中国自身的经验也体现了这种做法。 通过AI+计划，人工智能正在融入制造、医疗、物流、能源和消费服务领域，帮助打造全球最具活力的人工智能生态系统之一。 2025年，中国人工智能核心产业规模将超过1.2亿元人民币（约1300亿英镑），大量人工智能企业正在快速增长。

中国人工智能发展的另一个显着特点是重视开源、开放权重模型。 Qwen、DeepSeek 和 Kimi 等模型的成功表明，先进的人工智能功能可以以更低的成本开发，并可供更广泛的开发者和用户社区使用。 降低创新壁垒可以让更多国家、研究人员和小型企业参与人工智能革命，而不是被抛在后面。

需要强调的是，没有一个国家能够垄断创新。 不同国家在人工智能发展方面具有不同的优势，持久的进步将取决于这些优势如何相互补充，而不是孤立竞争。

这正是中英合作大有裨益的地方。 英国在前沿研究、生命科学、金融服务和人工智能创新等方面具有竞争优势。 中国在先进制造、工程和大规模工业部署方面拥有公认的优势，也是全球最大的人工智能应用市场之一。 这些优势是高度互补的。

在医疗保健领域，将英国在生物医学研究方面的优势与中国大规模部署人工智能的能力相结合，可以加速药物发现、改善医学成像并增强医疗保健服务。 在制造业中，将英国的创新与中国的工业能力相结合可以加速采用更智能、更清洁和更高效的生产。 联合研究还可以为人工智能安全、测试和评估的国际适用标准做出贡献，支持创新，同时增强公众信任。 这种合作不仅有利于我们两国，还能产生具有更广泛全球价值的解决方案。

中英两国政策制定者、研究人员和商界领袖需要加强交流，将对话转化为联合研究、商业伙伴关系以及在人工智能治理方面更密切的合作。

对于中国、英国以及更广泛的世界来说，合作不仅仅是可取的。 确保人工智能朝着造福人类的方向发展，才是正确的道路。
